content: HERC5, also known as probable E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase HERC5, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the HERC5 gene. This gene belongs to the HERC family of ubiquitin ligases and encodes a protein that contains a HECT domain and five RCC1 repeats. The expression of the HERC5 gene is upregulated in endothelial cells in response to pro-inflammatory cytokines. The HERC5 protein is localized to the cytoplasm and the perinuclear region, where it functions as an interferon-induced E3 protein ligase. Its primary role involves mediating ISGylation, a post-translational modification, of specific protein targets. The HERC5 gene is situated within a cluster of HERC family genes on chromosome 4. Functionally, HERC5 has demonstrated antiviral activity against several viruses, including HIV-1, influenza A virus, and human papillomavirus. In terms of molecular interactions, HERC5 has been shown to interact with NME2 (nucleoside diphosphate kinase B) and Cyclin E1, suggesting its involvement in various cellular processes.
